paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. The writer isn't trying to scare anybody. He's reminding the believers who they are and what they already have. "You, however, have an anointing from the Holy One, and all of you know the truth." (1 John 2:20) He wrote because they HAVE the truth, not because they lack it (1 John 2:21).

So what's the test? Whoever confesses the Son has the Father as well (1 John 2:23). Whoever denies that Jesus is the Christ is the one the writer calls the liar (1 John 2:22). Deceivers will show up, and I mean they WILL, but the writer says no lie comes from the truth (1 John 2:21). That means you don't have to be afraid of every new voice. You just have to know the real thing so well that the fake one sounds off.

And the real thing is not complicated, friend. "Let what you have heard from the beginning remain in you." (1 John 2:24) If it does, you will remain in the Son and in the Father, and the promise He made to us is eternal life (1 John 2:24-25). That's why I'm in this bakery every day with my hands in the Word, because staying in it is how you stay steady. So remain in Him, baker, and let the truth you've been taught keep you right where you belong (1 John 2:27).
